correctness.rationale: Bishop attack preserves parity r+c, so the whole independence complex is join X0*X1 of two actual diagonal-incidence bipartite matching/Ferrers complexes. Independent complete face enumeration and free tetrahedral collapse verified X0 f-by-size (1,13,46,46,8) and X1 (1,12,38,32,4), with respectively 8 and 4 free triangle-tetra pairs. After spanning-tree contraction independent exact word relator elimination canceled 33 of 34 generators in X0 leaving 1 circle plus five null 2-cells, and 25 of 27 in X1 leaving 2 circles plus three null 2-cells. Every elimination was checked as unique generator occurrence, giving integral homotopy equivalences, not just homology. Join distributes sphere counts to 2S3+13S4+15S5; full board face counts checked too.

originality.rationale: The bishop complex is equivalent to a join of two nonrectangular Ferrers-board matching complexes, but cited triangular Ferrers results require a row-length pattern absent here. Full rectangular chessboard/matching-complex torsion and independence-number formulas are not equivalent to these two explicit mixed CW types. No exact 5x5 bishop homotopy table was encountered in Resultary or primary comparisons.

Only the 5x5 ordinary board was assessed; general sizes and board topologies remain open.

value.rationale: The canonical ordinary 5x5 bishop-placement complex has a nontrivial mixed-dimensional integral sphere-wedge type, interesting in contrast to pure or single-dimensional shellable rook boards. The finite classification and its two parity-factor splittings are a natural exact invariant of this familiar graph-derived complex, with potentially reusable computation for neighboring board sizes.

final_claim: Integral mixed-sphere wedge of the nonattacking bishop 5-by-5 placement complex
